accrual.definition: An entry that books a cost or income in the period it belongs to, before the invoice or payment arrives.

award.definition: The amount a contract allows to be spent with a vendor; it can be raised, lowered or cancelled after signing.

budget-moment.definition: One of the points in a year at which a government publishes or revises its budget, from the draft budget through supplementary budgets to the annual report.

commitment.definition: Spending promised under a contract or order but not yet invoiced, which the budget already counts as used.

constant-currency.definition: Figures from different periods translated at one fixed set of exchange rates, so a change shows the business moving and not the rates.

days-to-pay.definition: The days from the date an invoice or voucher is entered to the date it is paid; it needs both dates for each payment.

duplicate-payment-rate.definition: The share of payments, by count or by amount, recorded more than once, whether paid twice or only listed twice.

fiscal-calendar.definition: How an entity splits its financial year into periods and when that year starts, such as January to December or April to March.

intercompany.definition: A transaction between two entities of the same group, which must be removed when their figures are added together.

legal-entity-identifier.definition: A 20-character code that names one legal entity worldwide, from a public register, used to tell apart vendors with similar names.

maker-checker.definition: A workflow where one identity prepares a change and a different identity approves it before it takes effect.

open-and-closed-period.definition: A period still taking entries is open; once closed, its figures are final and a change goes into a later open period instead.

outturn.definition: What was actually spent or received in a year, set against the budget for the same year.

paid-over-award.definition: What was paid on a contract beyond the award it is held to; never below zero, and never netted against what other contracts leave unpaid.

posting-date.definition: The date an entry counts in the ledger, which decides its fiscal period; it can differ from the document date and the payment date.

procure-to-pay.definition: The chain from agreeing to buy something to paying for it, through contract or order, invoice, voucher and payment.

record-to-report.definition: The chain from posting transactions in the ledger to publishing figures, through period close, reconciliation and consolidation.

reference-rate.definition: An exchange rate published by a central bank for one day, used to translate amounts between currencies the same way everywhere.

remaining-commitment.definition: The part of a contract's award not yet paid, which the award still allows to be spent; never below zero, since paying over an award leaves nothing to commit.

restatement.definition: A change to figures already published for a closed period, made and disclosed because they were wrong or a rule changed.

reversing-accrual.definition: An accrual that is undone automatically at the start of the next period, so the real invoice can be booked without counting the cost twice.

segregation-of-duties.definition: The rule that no one person both starts and approves the same transaction, so one mistake or fraud needs two people.

spend-against-award.definition: The share of a contract's award that has been paid so far; above one when the contract was paid more than it was awarded.

three-way-match.definition: The check that an invoice agrees with the order or contract and with what was received before it is paid.

trial-balance.definition: The list of every account's balance at one date; its debits and credits must add up to the same total.

voucher.definition: The approved record that an invoice may be paid, naming the vendor, the amount and the contract it is charged to.

chicago_payment_amount.description: Not for direct use: an input of `duplicate_payment_amount_rate`. The US dollars of the City of Chicago's payment rows as served, repeats included.
chicago_payment_amount.label: Chicago payments served, in dollars

chicago_payment_rows.description: Not for direct use: an input of `duplicate_payment_rate`. The City of Chicago's payment rows as served, repeats included.
chicago_payment_rows.label: Chicago payment rows served

chicago_repeat_amount.description: Not for direct use: an input of `duplicate_payment_amount_rate`. The US dollars of the City of Chicago's payment rows that repeat another served row.
chicago_repeat_amount.label: Chicago payments served again, in dollars

chicago_repeat_rows.description: Not for direct use: an input of `duplicate_payment_rate`. The City of Chicago's payment rows that repeat another served row.
chicago_repeat_rows.label: Chicago payment rows served again

constant_currency_spend.description: What the entities spent, in the reporting currency (EUR) at the ECB rates of one fixed day (the group totals' `constant_rates_on`), so a change between spans shows spending moving and not the rates: the group totals' figures, with what they leave out (`group_totals_left_out`) left out here too. It is a figure only where every row it sums has one basis, so group by `group_total__basis` (or by an entity with a single basis); a query that would add unlike bases, such as the Dutch cash outturn and Chicago's payments, returns no figure. A whole fiscal year's figure (the Dutch outturn, Chicago's yearly roll-ups) has no month: by `metric_time` the metric groups by year or coarser (a basis of whole years also shows a row with no time and no figure), and a query by month or day is refused; by `group_total__period_start` a whole year's row has no month and stands apart. For months, group by `group_total__fiscal_year` and `group_total__fiscal_period` (no period on a whole year's row); `group_total__span` tells the two kinds of row apart.
constant_currency_spend.label: Constant-currency spend

type_params.expr: case when coalesce(spend_bases_in_periods, 0) + coalesce(spend_bases_in_years, 0) = 1 then coalesce(spend_in_periods, 0) + coalesce(spend_in_years, 0) end

verified_queries.question: What was spent on each basis, in euros at constant rates?
verified_queries.sql:
select
  basis as group_total__basis,
  case
    when count(distinct case when fiscal_period is not null then basis end)
      + count(distinct case when fiscal_period is null then basis end) = 1
    then coalesce(sum(amount_at_constant_rates), 0)
  end as constant_currency_spend
from group_totals
group by basis

verified_queries.question: What was spent on each basis in each fiscal year, in euros at constant rates?
verified_queries.sql:
select
  basis as group_total__basis,
  fiscal_year as group_total__fiscal_year,
  case
    when count(distinct case when fiscal_period is not null then basis end)
      + count(distinct case when fiscal_period is null then basis end) = 1
    then coalesce(sum(amount_at_constant_rates), 0)
  end as constant_currency_spend
from group_totals
group by basis, fiscal_year

verified_queries.question: What did each entity spend, in euros at constant rates, where all its figures share one basis?
verified_queries.sql:
select
  entity_id as group_total__entity_id,
  case
    when count(distinct case when fiscal_period is not null then basis end)
      + count(distinct case when fiscal_period is null then basis end) = 1
    then coalesce(sum(amount_at_constant_rates), 0)
  end as constant_currency_spend
from group_totals
group by entity_id

duplicate_payment_amount_rate.description: The share of the dollars the City of Chicago's served payment rows add up to that sits on rows repeating another served row: the publisher serving one payment twice, not the City paying twice. Chicago only, the one entity with a rule for repeats.
duplicate_payment_amount_rate.label: Duplicate-payment rate by amount

verified_queries.question: What share of the dollars of the City of Chicago's served payment rows sits on rows that repeat another served row?
verified_queries.sql:
select
  cast(sum(case when is_repeat then amount else 0 end) as double)
    / cast(nullif(sum(amount), 0) as double) as duplicate_payment_amount_rate
from payments
where entity_id = 'chicago'

duplicate_payment_rate.description: The share of the City of Chicago's served payment rows that repeat another served row (`is_repeat`): the publisher serving one payment twice, not the City paying twice, which nothing in the files shows. Chicago only, the one entity with a rule for repeats.
duplicate_payment_rate.label: Duplicate-payment rate

verified_queries.question: What share of the City of Chicago's served payment rows repeat another served row?
verified_queries.sql:
select
  cast(sum(case when is_repeat then 1 else 0 end) as double)
    / cast(nullif(count(payment_key), 0) as double) as duplicate_payment_rate
from payments
where entity_id = 'chicago'

verified_queries.question: By month of payment date, what share of the City of Chicago's served payment rows repeat another served row?
verified_queries.sql:
select
  date_trunc('month', payment_date) as metric_time__month,
  cast(sum(case when is_repeat then 1 else 0 end) as double)
    / cast(nullif(count(payment_key), 0) as double) as duplicate_payment_rate
from payments
where entity_id = 'chicago'
group by date_trunc('month', payment_date)

fixed_award.description: Not for direct use: the denominator of `spend_against_award`. The awards held to of the City of Chicago's contracts with a fixed award (above 0), in US dollars, by approval cohort.
fixed_award.label: Fixed award

paid_against_fixed_award.description: Not for direct use: the numerator of `spend_against_award`. What was paid against the City of Chicago's contracts with a fixed award (above 0), every repeat left out, in US dollars, by approval cohort.
paid_against_fixed_award.label: Paid against fixed award

paid_over_award.description: What the City of Chicago paid beyond the award on contracts with a fixed award (an award held to above 0): per contract, the reconciliation's difference where it is above 0, summed, the rounding allowance not taken off; the part `remaining_commitment` never nets away. By `metric_time` it groups contracts by approval cohort (the day of their first revision), not by when the excess was paid. Group by `contract__break_class` for the cause the reconciliation finds.
paid_over_award.label: Paid over award

verified_queries.question: How much did Chicago pay beyond the award on its fixed-award contracts, by the reconciliation's break class?
verified_queries.sql:
select
  break_class as contract__break_class,
  sum(
    case when award_held_to > 0 then
      case when difference > 0 then difference else 0 end
    end
  ) as paid_over_award
from chicago_contract_reconciliation
group by break_class

remaining_commitment.description: The part of the City of Chicago's fixed contract awards not yet paid: per contract with a fixed award (an award held to above 0), the award held to less what was paid against it, never below 0, summed; what contracts were paid beyond their award is `paid_over_award`, never netted here. It is what the awards still allow, not money owed or due, and it holds expired contracts: on the pinned files $71.38bn, of which $31.80bn sits on 63,490 contracts whose latest end date is before the files' cut-off (31 October 2026), $10.98bn on 19,116 that serve no end date and $28.60bn on 3,612 still running; filter on `contract__last_ends_on` for those. By `metric_time` it groups contracts by approval cohort (the day of their first revision): "by year" is what each year's newly awarded contracts still allow, not a balance at the end of that year.
remaining_commitment.label: Remaining commitment

verified_queries.question: How much of the City of Chicago's fixed contract awards is not yet paid?
verified_queries.sql:
select
  sum(
    case when award_held_to > 0 then
      case when paid < award_held_to then award_held_to - paid else 0 end
    end
  ) as remaining_commitment
from chicago_contract_reconciliation

verified_queries.question: How much of the fixed awards of Chicago's contracts still running on 31 October 2026 is not yet paid?
verified_queries.sql:
select
  sum(
    case when award_held_to > 0 then
      case when paid < award_held_to then award_held_to - paid else 0 end
    end
  ) as remaining_commitment
from chicago_contract_reconciliation
where last_ends_on >= date '2026-10-31'

spend_against_award.description: The share of the City of Chicago's fixed contract awards that has been paid: what was paid against contracts with a fixed award (an award held to above 0, as the contract reconciliation holds it: the award after revisions, or the highest award ever in force where revisions net to 0 without all being 0), every repeat left out, over those awards. Left out: a blanket whose every revision awards 0, a negative award, a contract number the contracts table lacks, and the contracts whose revisions net to 0 and whose award never rose above 0 (24 classed `unexplained`, 197 `unpaid` on the pinned files). A contract paid over its award counts its whole payment, so a group of contracts can pass 1. By `metric_time` it groups contracts by approval cohort (the day of their first revision), not by when they were paid. Group by `contract__break_class` to see where it comes from.
spend_against_award.label: Spend against award

verified_queries.question: What share of the City of Chicago's fixed contract awards has been paid?
verified_queries.sql:
select
  cast(sum(case when award_held_to > 0 then paid end) as double)
    / cast(nullif(sum(case when award_held_to > 0 then award_held_to end), 0) as double)
    as spend_against_award
from chicago_contract_reconciliation

verified_queries.question: What share of the fixed awards of the contracts Chicago first approved in each year has been paid?
verified_queries.sql:
select
  date_trunc('year', first_approved_on) as metric_time__year,
  cast(sum(case when award_held_to > 0 then paid end) as double)
    / cast(nullif(sum(case when award_held_to > 0 then award_held_to end), 0) as double)
    as spend_against_award
from chicago_contract_reconciliation
group by date_trunc('year', first_approved_on)

spend_bases_in_periods.description: Not for direct use: an input of `constant_currency_spend`. How many different bases the summed fiscal periods' rows hold.
spend_bases_in_periods.label: Bases summed in fiscal periods

spend_bases_in_years.description: Not for direct use: an input of `constant_currency_spend`. How many different bases the summed whole fiscal years' rows hold.
spend_bases_in_years.label: Bases summed in whole fiscal years

spend_in_periods.description: Not for direct use: an input of `constant_currency_spend`, which is the figure to read. The fiscal periods' figures at constant rates summed whatever their basis, so on its own it adds unlike bases.
spend_in_periods.label: Spend at constant rates in fiscal periods, any basis

spend_in_years.description: Not for direct use: an input of `constant_currency_spend`, which is the figure to read. The whole fiscal years' figures at constant rates summed whatever their basis, so on its own it adds unlike bases.
spend_in_years.label: Spend at constant rates in whole fiscal years, any basis
